steps.title: Calculate a signed moment
steps.explanation: A 5 kg load exerts 49.05 N downward in the authored 9.81 m/s² field. The 0.30 m lever is horizontal, so τz = rx Fy = 0.30 × (−49.05) = −14.715 N m. Positive z is counterclockwise viewed toward the origin.
steps.observe: Moment arm = 0.30 m and torque = −14.715 N m. A static pose would require an external +14.715 N m hold moment.

steps.title: Separate lever length from moment arm
steps.explanation: Rotate the same 0.30 m lever to 60°. Its horizontal offset is 0.30 cos 60° = 0.15 m, even though its length is unchanged. Gravity acts along the grey vertical line; the orange horizontal segment is the perpendicular offset.
steps.observe: Moment arm = 0.15 m and torque = −7.3575 N m: exactly half the horizontal-case magnitude within floating-point precision.

steps.title: Put gravity through the pivot
steps.explanation: At 90°, gravity’s line of action passes through the pivot. The force is still 49.05 N, but its perpendicular offset is zero. This is a posed geometric calculation, not a prediction that the lever stays there without supports.
steps.observe: Torque is approximately −9.01 × 10⁻¹⁶ N m and moment arm approximately 1.84 × 10⁻¹⁷ m: numerical zero, not a small physical moment.

steps.title: Cross the pivot and reverse the moment
steps.explanation: At 120° the load is left of the pivot: rx = −0.15 m. Multiplying this negative offset by the downward force gives a positive moment. The unsigned moment-arm magnitude alone cannot tell you the rotation direction.
steps.observe: Moment-arm magnitude remains 0.15 m, but torque is now +7.3575 N m. The required static hold moment reverses to −7.3575 N m.

audit.finding: The ±80° adapter bound excluded the chapter’s zero moment at 90° and sign reversal at 120°. It showed no force line of action or supporting hold moment.
audit.change: Expanded only the presentation control to ±120°, and added the perpendicular offset, gravity line and required external static hold diagnostic.
audit.remaining: Prescribed planar massless lever; no angular trajectory, support reaction solve, joint mechanics or anatomical coordinate claim.
